evals.prompt: Use /pr-explainer on Azure DevOps PR 41 in the current repository. Create an HTML walkthrough that explains the starter-credit registration race, includes production timing evidence when available, and compares before/after request ordering.
evals.expected_output: A standalone HTML file under ./output/ with the exact PR-explainer section order, red before-flow problem highlights, green after-flow fix highlights, and both simplified and UML sequence diagrams.
expectations: The final HTML is written under ./output/.
The HTML contains two simplified sequence diagrams and two detailed UML sequence diagrams.
The old flow has red problem highlights and the fixed flow has green highlights.
The document includes a scope boundary and changed-file explanation cards.
Production evidence is included only when retrieved from a real source.

evals.prompt: Explain my current staged and unstaged changes with /pr-explainer. There is no PR yet. Compare HEAD to the working tree and create the HTML in output.
evals.expected_output: A local-change explainer under ./output/ based on the actual working-tree diff, with previous/current flows and no invented PR metadata.
expectations: The skill uses local-change mode and does not require a PR.
The filename identifies the artifact as a local-change explainer.
The previous state is derived from HEAD and the fixed state from the working tree.
The HTML contains red and green flow highlights plus changed-file cards.
No runtime evidence section is fabricated when none exists.

evals.prompt: Explicitly trigger pr-explainer for an additive feature that introduces audit-log export. There was no bug or incident, just a missing capability. Show the previous manual workflow and the new automated flow, but do not pretend there was production failure evidence.
evals.expected_output: An HTML explainer that treats the old state as a capability gap, marks only the gap red, marks only implemented automation green, and omits unsupported evidence.
expectations: The old flow is framed as a missing capability rather than an invented defect.
The scope boundary distinguishes the feature from adjacent work.
The evidence section is omitted or explicitly states that no runtime evidence exists.
Both simplified and detailed sequence diagrams are present.
Only changed solution steps are highlighted green.
